canonical_policy.name: Use TimeProvider for testable current-time logic
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Use TimeProvider for application logic that depends on the current clock and needs deterministic testing; do not mechanically replace explicit/stored timestamps.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Clock-dependent deterministic test TimeProvider default and stored-date exception matches; explicit test wallclock restriction0170, default issueBF0091.

context_quotes:
- Tests must be deterministic, independent of execution order, and isolated from Production and Development data, uncontrolled external systems and shared mutable state, and must not rely on wall-clock timing when `TimeProvider` can make time deterministic. Never connect automated tests to Production data.
- Tests must start from a known state and own their setup; they must not depend on development seeding or on test execution order.

- Default: use `TimeProvider` for application logic whose behavior depends on the current clock and needs deterministic tests. Stored timestamps and explicit dates are not clock dependencies; do not replace every `DateTime`/`DateTimeOffset` mechanically.

Configure the `Testing` environment with isolated test resources so an integration test cannot reach a development or production database by accident (`rules/backend-tests/testing.md` § Isolation and data). If top-level statements make `Program` inaccessible, expose it, for example with a `public partial class Program` declaration.

At the relevant boundary use a fake or mock abstraction (unit tests), a stub `HttpMessageHandler`, WireMock or another local fake server (HTTP integration), or a dedicated sandbox only when the test explicitly targets that integration. Keep slow or unreliable external-system tests separate from ordinary fast runs.

Testing private details; mocking every class; hitting production resources; shared mutable state; assertions that repeat the implementation; assertion-free tests (unless the behavior is "does not throw"); `Task.Delay` to make timing-sensitive tests pass; Testcontainers without a provider-fidelity need; EF InMemory while claiming relational coverage.
|---|---|
| Pure business rule | NUnit unit test |
| Application orchestration | Unit test with controlled boundary doubles when useful |
| Full API pipeline | `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` |
| Important EF/provider behavior | Integration test with the actual provider |
| Simple API integration, provider irrelevant | Lightweight isolated relational test DB may suffice |
| Time-dependent behavior | `TimeProvider` / `FakeTimeProvider` |
| External HTTP dependency | Stub handler or local fake server |
| Reproduced bug | Focused regression test |
| Temporary behavioral probe | Maintained test or confirmed existing coverage |
| Deployment/basic health | Smoke test |

Projection is not mandatory when the use case genuinely needs the entity, but avoid loading a whole aggregate to return two scalar fields.

Use tracking queries when loaded entities will be modified and committed through the current Unit of Work, and `AsNoTracking()` for read-only entity queries where tracking adds nothing. Projections to non-entity DTOs do not need `AsNoTracking()`.

Make the query shape explicit: projection for selected related data, `Include`/`ThenInclude` when the entity graph itself is required. canonical_policy.name: Caching requires concrete semantics/need
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Caching is not a default architecture requirement; introduce it only for a clear measured/reasoned need and choose implementation according to deployment, consistency and staleness requirements.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Reasoned/measured need matches; performance-only measurement stronger clause already0295/BF0062; consistency firstEXTRA0090 and expiration factors0300.

context_quotes:
- Default: caching is an optimization, not an architecture requirement. Introduce it only for a clear measured or reasoned need — expensive repeated work, high read volume, expensive remote calls with acceptable staleness — and choose the implementation by deployment, consistency and staleness requirements, never merely because a value is read often.
- Cache technology must stay out of Domain, and infrastructure cache APIs must not leak into Application without a deliberate boundary abstraction.

Define consistency semantics first — how stale data may become and how it is invalidated — and measure before adding caching purely for performance.

A distributed backend such as Redis is added only when deployment requirements justify it.

Choose by data semantics, not a universal default: change frequency, regeneration cost, acceptable staleness, memory footprint, behavior when the source is unavailable.

Caching by default without a reason; global keys for tenant/user data; indefinitely cached mutable data; cache technology in Domain; Application depending directly on `HybridCache` without a deliberate decision; caching EF tracked entities across Unit of Work boundaries; cache as authoritative persistence; Redis added merely because caching exists.

| Need | Consideration |
|---|---|
| Entire reusable HTTP response | ASP.NET Core output caching |
| Local application cache | In-memory or HybridCache |
| Multi-instance shared cache | Distributed cache / HybridCache L2 (Reserved) |
| Expensive repeated remote read | Cache in Infrastructure when the contract permits |
| Application-controlled invalidation | Application abstraction + Infrastructure implementation |
| Unknown performance problem | Measure first |
